expectations.text: The prompt explicitly specifies a gray / neutral-gray background
expectations.evidence: 'on a plain neutral light-gray seamless background'.

expectations.text: The prompt requests 3 or more views of the remote on one sheet (e.g., front, back, side, three-quarter)
expectations.evidence: Primary prompt is a single view: 'shot straight-on from above (top-down view)'. The only other view is an 'Optional second angle' generated as a separate image ('If your video model accepts multiple reference images, generate a matching 3/4 perspective view') — two views total, and not on one sheet.

expectations.text: The prompt includes physical-volume cues: cast shadows AND studio reflections (or equivalent surface-realism language)
expectations.evidence: The prompt actually suppresses shadows: 'soft even lighting, no shadows cutting across the buttons'. No cast shadows or studio reflections are requested anywhere; surface language is limited to 'matte... plastic body' and 'glossy red rubber' button texture.

expectations.text: A literal red arrow marking the power button is included — either prompted into the sheet or as an explicit edit-pass instruction
expectations.evidence: No arrow of any kind appears in either prompt or the guidance; disambiguation relies only on verbal cues ('five redundant disambiguators (largest button, top-center position, red color...)').

expectations.text: QA guidance includes rejecting flat / 2D-looking results
expectations.evidence: QA item (5) checks 'the remote reads as thick/chunky, not a slim modern remote' — a prop-design check, not a rejection criterion for flat/2D-looking renders. No flat/sticker-like/2D rejection guidance exists.

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions — this eval cleanly separates skill behavior (multi-view sheet, volume cues, red-arrow annotation, flatness QA) from a competent baseline.
